glosses: A short-horned goat antelope native to mountainous terrain in southern Europe; Rupicapra rupicapra.

examples.text: When my father returned from Milan, he found playing with me in the hall of our villa a child fairer than pictured cherub – a creature who seemed to shed radiance from her looks and whose form and motions were lighter than the chamois of the hills.

glosses: Ellipsis of chamois leather (“soft pliable leather originally made from the skin of chamois (nowadays the hides of deer, sheep, and other species of goat are alternatively used)”).

examples.text: [H]e seldom donned his armour, substituted costly damask and silk for his war-worn shamoy doublet, and affected at his advanced time of life more gaiety of attire than his contemporaries remembered as distinguishing his early youth.

glosses: The traditional colour of chamois leather.
An absorbent cloth used for cleaning and polishing, formerly made of chamois leather.

examples.text: I took them, breathed on them, polished them with a chamois and hung them on the chandelier.
Mirrors can be cleaned with warm water and ammonia or vinegar and polished with a chamois.
Once your paint has been restored, drying your car with a chamois is just about all you have to do to restore the luster.

glosses: A padded insert which protects the groin from the bicycle saddle.
To clean with a chamois leather cloth.

examples.text: Jak kamzík skáče po stráních, divá se dolů, propukne v smích, směje se v horstvu svobodném dítěti, ženě, muži a všem,...
